title: Advancing Functional Safety: Improving Failure Mode Analysis and Fault Injection Using Automation and GNN Algorithms
problem: Complex electronic systems require Failure Mode Analysis and Fault Injection for functional safety, but traditional methods suffer from high simulation time, manual effort, and scalability challenges.
motivation: High-reliability systems need efficient FMA and FI processes. Growing design complexity makes manual analysis impractical and error-prone. Need for automation and accelerated fault criticality detection.
method: Two-part solution: (1) FMA automation system ensuring consistency and reducing manual effort, (2) GNN-based acceleration of FI process using GCNII model to detect critical nodes and predict fault criticality.
key_novelty: Application of GCNII Graph Neural Networks to functional safety verification; overcomes limitations of traditional GCN in handling complex designs with higher logic depth.
contributions: FMA automation system for consistency and effort reduction
GNN-based (GCNII) fault criticality detection and prediction
Acceleration of fault injection process for complex designs
Improved accuracy in forecasting fault impact
limitations: Abstract only; no quantitative results on acceleration factor or accuracy metrics; no comparison with other ML approaches.
